neighbours.label: A comparative claim about how a vehicle or vessel behaves after a change ('makes the boat more stable', 'harder to park', 'to improve yaw control', 'improved grip'), firing on the comparative or 'improve(d)' or the 'to' after it; the same vehicles described without a comparison, and comparative claims about non-vehicles (doors, phones, houses), stay low.
fire: A longer hull makes the canoe faster in open water.
The extra weight makes the van slower to accelerate.
Fitting a stabiliser keeps the yacht steadier in waves.
Low-profile tyres make the car noisier on motorways.
A bigger rudder was fitted to improve the ship's turning.
The narrow frame makes the bicycle easier to carry.
Raising the wing gives the glider improved lift at low speed.
The heavy trailer makes the pickup harder to stop.
quiet: The canoe has a long hull and two seats.
The van carries extra weight in the back.
The yacht has a stabiliser and a blue sail.
The car came with low-profile tyres.
The ship has a large rudder at the stern.
A larger lock makes the gate harder to open.
Thicker glass makes the phone screen safer to drop.
Double glazing keeps the flat quieter at night.

short: comparative claim about a vehicle's behaviour
notes: Round 2 for this pole (round 1, sweep 3: 'improving a vehicle's stability / handling' failed with 2 near misses: 'makes the truck harder to park' 0.67, 'makes the scooter cheaper to build' 0.35). Refinement probe: 'makes the boat more stable' 0.63; non-vehicle comparatives lower ('door easier to open' 0.18, 'house warmer' 0.13, 'phone heavier' 0.05); vehicles without comparison 0.01-0.03. New label: any comparative claim about a vehicle, better or worse.
